title: An agent records what a pane draws as a video or GIF
body:
decade's `screenshot` MCP tool and its `screenshot` socket verb each capture one frame of what a pane draws, as a PNG, in `decade/src/server/compositor/screenshot.rs`. A README for a terminal program needs motion too: a picker moving through a list, a bar filling up, a pointer selecting text. GitHub and crates.io both play a GIF embedded in a README.

## Proposal

### Permission

- The two per-pane modes, accept screenshots and accept saved screenshots, merge into one mode that covers viewing, saving and recording. The pane keeps one button and one tag, the camera.
- A screenshot or a recording without the mode asks in the existing dialog, and allowing one repeatedly allows the other.

### Requests

- An MCP tool `record` takes an absolute path. A socket verb `record` sits behind `decade record PANE FILE [flags]`, which makes a relative path absolute, as `decade screenshot` does.
- The request carries `format` (`mp4` or `gif`, matching the file's extension), `fps` (default 30 for mp4, 15 for gif), `duration` in seconds, `width` (default the pane's width, height following the aspect ratio), `quality` (mp4 only, mapped to ffmpeg's crf), `pointer` (default on) and `loop` (gif only).
- A recording ends at its duration, at a hard cap of 5 minutes, on a stop call, or when the pane closes, its tab or workspace stops being shown, or the requester disconnects. decade keeps what it captured in every case.
- decade refuses the call when `ffmpeg` is not on its `PATH`, when the file exists, when its directory does not, and when the pane already records.
- The output only goes to a file. decade holds no frames beyond the one being written.

### Capture

- decade renders the pane at the requested rate, with the same offscreen render `screenshot` uses, and writes each frame as raw video to an `ffmpeg` child process on its stdin. A tick with no change repeats the last frame. A GIF goes through ffmpeg's two-pass palette.
- A pane resized mid-recording is scaled or letterboxed to the size the recording started at.
- decade draws the pointer into the frames while it is over the pane, unless `pointer` is false.
- When ffmpeg fails, the error carries the last lines of its stderr.

### While recording

- The pane shows a red blinking recording icon, like a camcorder's, and its outline pulses red.
- The pane's frame shows how long the recording has run.

## Rejected

- `vhs` drives a terminal in headless Chrome from a script. Its script has no mouse commands, so it cannot show selecting or clicking.
- `asciinema` with `agg` draws the terminal again with `agg`'s own glyph renderer, not the terminal's. It shows no pointer.
- `gpu-screen-recorder` on a region of the screen needs the pane's region found by hand, and the region moves with the layout.
- A separate accept mode for recording. Jack wants one mechanism for every capture.
- An encoder inside decade. decade hands frames to the `ffmpeg` command and will not grow its own encoding.
close_reason: Landed in 0b9cd00, e9d73b4 and 47420c6, merged into dev as 10d8d65. Jack has not yet seen the recording icon, the red pulse or the elapsed-time tag on a live server, and ffmpeg runs with its default thread count.
